S03_00.text: It feels like the simplest idea in the world: everyone, everywhere, shares the same now.

S03_01.text: Everyone, everywhere, shares the same now.

S04_01.text: And strictly speaking, it is not true.

S05_00.text: In 1905, Einstein began with two facts that had been measured, but not understood.

S06_00.text: The laws of physics look the same to anyone moving at constant velocity.

S06_01.text: And light, in empty space, always moves at the same speed, whoever is measuring it.

S07_00.text: Hold on to both at once, and something has to give.

S07_01.text: What gives is the idea of a shared now.

S08_00.text: Picture a flash of light released from the exact middle of a moving ship.

S08_01.text: For someone on board, it reaches the front and the back at the same instant.

S09_00.text: For someone watching the ship pass, the back wall rushes toward the light, and the front wall runs away from it.

S09_01.text: The flash reaches the back first.

S10_01.text: The order of distant events depends on how you are moving, and no experiment can settle which of them is right.

S10_02.text: No experiment, anywhere, can settle which of them is right.

S11_00.text: Follow the consequences, and the familiar structure of time comes apart.

S12_00.text: A moving clock ticks more slowly, as measured by someone it moves past.

S12_01.text: A moving ruler is shorter along its direction of travel.

S12_02.text: These are not illusions. They are measurements.

S13_00.text: To see why, physicists draw a map that no one can walk on.

S13_01.text: Space along one axis. Time along the other.

S14_00.text: Every clock traces a line through this map: its world line.

S14_01.text: And everything that can ever influence an event, or be influenced by it, lies inside two cones of light.

S15_00.text: Outside the cones lies a vast region of events that are neither before nor after.

S15_01.text: For them, 'now' is simply not defined.

S16_00.text: Change your velocity, and the slice you call 'the present' tilts.

S16_01.text: What happens 'at the same time' on a distant star is, quite literally, a matter of perspective.

S17_00.text: This is not philosophy. It is measured every day.

S17_01.text: Clocks aboard GPS satellites gain about thirty-eight microseconds a day on clocks on the ground.

S17_02.text: Left uncorrected, your position would drift by kilometers within a day.

S18_01.text: Follow a single pulse, and you can measure the universe with it.

S19_00.text: Across an atom, it takes less than a billionth of a billionth of a second.

S20_00.text: Across a human body, a few billionths of a second.

S21_00.text: Around the Earth, seven times in one second.

S22_00.text: To the Moon, a little over a second.

S22_02.text: To the Voyager probes, most of a day.

S23_00.text: To the nearest star, four years.

S23_01.text: Across our galaxy, a hundred thousand years.

S23_02.text: To the farthest light we can see, more than thirteen billion years.

S24_00.text: Every image of the sky is a layered photograph of different pasts.

S24_01.text: There is no single 'now' out there to look at.

S25_00.text: Then Einstein asked a harder question.

S25_01.text: What happens to this map when gravity is present?

S26_01.text: Gravity is not a force pulling through space. It is the shape of space and time themselves.

S27_00.text: Mass tells spacetime how to curve.

S28_00.text: A planet in orbit is not being pulled.

S28_01.text: It is travelling as straight as it can through a geometry that is bent.

S29_01.text: A galaxy behind a massive cluster is smeared into arcs and rings: a lens made of pure gravity.

S30_00.text: And clocks run at different rates depending on where they sit in that geometry.

S30_01.text: Deeper in a gravitational well, time runs slower.

S30_02.text: In 2010, two atomic clocks, one raised just thirty-three centimeters above the other, measurably disagreed.

S31_00.text: Compress enough mass into a small enough region, and there is a boundary from which no path leads back out. Not even for light.

S31_01.text: We call it the event horizon.

S35_00.text: And around the shadow, a thin bright ring: light that circled the black hole before escaping.

S35_01.text: In 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope saw that ring around the black hole in the galaxy M87; in 2022, around the one at the center of our own.

S36_00.text: At the horizon, seen from far away, a falling clock seems to slow, and stop.

S36_01.text: For the one who falls, nothing special marks the crossing.

S36_03.text: There is no now they could share.

S37_00.text: While relativity was redrawing the large, a different revolution was dismantling the small.

S38_00.text: An electron in an atom is not a tiny planet on a tiny orbit.

S38_01.text: It is better described by a wave of possibility: a cloud whose shape is the solution of an equation.

S39_00.text: Where the wave is dense, the electron is likely to be found.

S39_01.text: Where it cancels itself, it is never found.

S40_00.text: A quantum system can be in a superposition: not here or there, but a precise blend of both, with amplitudes that add and subtract like waves.

S40_01.text: Measure it, and you get one definite answer.

S40_02.text: Repeat it, and the answers follow the probabilities the wave predicted.

S41_00.text: And some pairs of questions cannot both have sharp answers.

S41_01.text: The more precisely a position is fixed, the less precisely momentum can be.

S41_02.text: This is not a limit of instruments. It is a property of waves.

S42_00.text: Now take two particles, prepared together, so that their properties are linked.

S46_00.text: So we arrive at the strangest situation in modern science.

S47_00.text: On one side, general relativity: gravity as geometry.

S47_01.text: It predicted the bending of starlight, the slowing of clocks, black holes, and the gravitational waves first detected in 2015.

S48_00.text: On the other, quantum field theory: particles as excitations of fields filling all of space.

S48_01.text: It predicts the magnetism of the electron to twelve decimal places.

S49_00.text: Each works, in its domain, to a precision that is almost absurd. But they speak different languages.

S49_01.text: In relativity, spacetime is a smooth, dynamic stage, shaped by the matter on it.

S49_02.text: In quantum theory, the stage is fixed, and the actors are uncertain.

S49_03.text: In quantum theory, the stage is fixed, and the actors are uncertain.

S50_00.text: Try to make gravity itself quantum, the way the other forces are, and the calculations fill with infinities the usual methods cannot tame.

S50_01.text: At ordinary energies this is harmless: each theory is used where it applies.

S50_02.text: But at the center of a black hole, and in the first instant of the universe, both must matter at once.

S50_03.text: There, our best descriptions stop making predictions.

S51_00.text: What is reality made of, at the deepest level?

S52_03.text: Ideas in which space and time themselves emerge from something deeper, the way temperature emerges from the motion of molecules.

S53_00.text: None of them has yet made a prediction that experiment has confirmed.

S53_01.text: They are not established physics. They are the frontier.

S54_02.text: Time is local, and relative, and shaped by mass.

S54_03.text: At the smallest scales, reality is probabilistic, and correlated in ways that have no classical explanation.

S54_04.text: And our two best theories, each confirmed beyond reasonable doubt, do not yet fit together.

S55_00.text: So return to the first clock.

S55_01.text: Are these two events happening at the same time?

S56_00.text: The question that seemed trivial was never trivial.

S56_01.text: It depends on where you stand, how you move, and what you are near.

S56_02.text: And the universe, as far as we can tell, keeps no single time for anyone.
